title: Blob containers and Azure file shares
learningObjective: Create and set up blob containers (names, anonymous access) and file shares (protocol, tier, size limit, mounting).
foundation: Blob Storage keeps objects (files of any kind) in containers, which are like top-level folders in a storage account.
Azure Files offers file shares that computers mount like a network drive using SMB (Windows, Linux, macOS) or NFS (Linux).
Containers are private by default. You can allow anonymous read access only if the storage account allows it.
engineer: Container names: 3 to 63 characters; lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens; start with a letter or number; no two hyphens in a row.
Folders in blob storage: a '/' in a blob name only looks like a folder. Real folders exist only with hierarchical namespace.

Anonymous access levels: Private, the default, with no anonymous access; Blob, where anyone with the URL can read a blob; Container, where anyone can read and also list the blobs. Blob and Container only appear if the account allows blob anonymous access.
Blob types: block blobs, for most data; append blobs, for logs (you only add to the end); page blobs, for random reads and writes, such as VHD disks.
Container features: immutability policies (time-based retention, legal hold); metadata; stored access policies.
Standard file shares (on Standard GPv2 accounts): pay as you go, with three tiers: Transaction optimized, Hot and Cool. SMB only. Size limit 5 TiB, or up to 100 TiB with large file shares turned on.
Premium file shares (on FileStorage accounts): you pay for the size you reserve (provisioned). SMB or NFS 4.1. Up to 100 TiB.
Mounting a share: SMB uses TCP port 445. The share's Connect page gives you a ready script (net use on Windows, mount on Linux). If port 445 is blocked, use a private endpoint or VPN.
Azure File Sync: keeps a copy (cache) of the share on your own Windows Servers.
Hierarchical namespace (Data Lake Storage Gen2): containers become file systems, with real folders, POSIX permissions (ACLs) and a dfs endpoint.

example.title: Website images and team shares
body: Marketing serves product images from a container with Blob-level anonymous access. It's in its own storage account, the only one where anonymous access is allowed, and Azure Front Door sits in front.
The finance team's share 'finance' (Hot tier, 2 TiB limit) is mounted as drive Z: on their PCs, through a private endpoint, with identity-based access.

prerequisites: A storage account of the right type
Anonymous access allowed on the account, for public containers
permissions: Storage Blob Data Contributor (data) or Contributor (management), to create containers
Storage Account Contributor, to create file shares
limits: Container and share names: 3 to 63 characters
Standard share: 5 TiB, or 100 TiB with large file shares
portal: Storage account > Data storage > Containers > + Container: name and anonymous access level.
Data storage > File shares > + File share: name, tier (Transaction optimized/Hot/Cool or premium provisioned), protocol (premium), quota; backup option.
File share > Connect: choose OS and drive letter, copy the script.
configuration.cli:
az storage container create --account-name stcontoso01 --name reports --auth-mode login --public-access off
az storage account update -g rg-data -n stcontoso01 --enable-large-file-share
az storage share-rm create -g rg-data --storage-account stcontoso01 --name finance --quota 2048 --access-tier Hot
az storage share-rm create -g rg-data --storage-account stpremfiles --name linuxdata --quota 1024 --enabled-protocols NFS
configuration.powershell:
$ctx = New-AzStorageContext -StorageAccountName stcontoso01 -UseConnectedAccount
New-AzStorageContainer -Name reports -Context $ctx -Permission Off
New-AzRmStorageShare -ResourceGroupName rg-data -StorageAccountName stcontoso01 -Name finance -QuotaGiB 2048 -AccessTier Hot
net use Z: \\stcontoso01.file.core.windows.net\finance

lab.cost: None in the simulation. Standard shares are billed by used capacity and transactions; premium shares by provisioned size.

troubleshooting.symptom: The anonymous access options are greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: The account has 'Allow blob anonymous access' turned off.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn it on for the account (if your rules allow it), or use a SAS or Entra ID.

troubleshooting.cause: The container is Private. Anonymous requests get 404, not 403.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the level to Blob, or use a SAS.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't set a share's size limit above 5 TiB.
troubleshooting.cause: Large file shares isn't turned on.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on large file shares. You can't turn it off again.

troubleshooting.symptom: Mounting an NFS share on Linux fails.
troubleshooting.cause: NFS needs a premium share and private network access, and has its own secure-transfer rules.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a FileStorage account with a private endpoint or service endpoint, and follow the NFS mounting steps.

comparisons.difference: An S3 bucket is like a container (but each bucket name is global). EFS (NFS) and FSx are like Azure file shares.

misconceptions.myth: Normal blob storage has real folders.
misconceptions.reality: No. Folders are just parts of the blob name, unless hierarchical namespace is on.

misconceptions.myth: Any storage account can have NFS shares.
misconceptions.reality: No. NFS needs premium file shares.

architectureDecisions: Public files get their own account: then anonymous access can stay off everywhere else.
Pick shares by need: premium for low latency or NFS, standard Hot or Cool for ordinary file shares.

walkthrough.subtitle: Two ways to store files: blob containers for apps and the web, file shares for drives that people and servers mount.
learn: Anonymous access is off by default
Azure file shares: SMB and NFS

steps.label: Two needs
steps.title: Images for a website, and a shared drive for staff
body: The website needs files reachable by URL. Staff want a drive letter like the old file server.

steps.label: Containers
steps.title: Blob containers hold objects
body: A container groups blobs, like a folder. Its access level is Private (default), Blob (anyone can read blobs if they know the URL) or Container (anyone can also list the blobs).

steps.label: Anonymous
steps.title: Public access needs two switches
body: Anonymous read works only if the account allows anonymous access (off by default) and the container's level is Blob or Container.

callout.text: Most data should stay Private. Use SAS links or a CDN for sharing.

steps.label: File shares
steps.title: File shares behave like a network drive
body: Azure Files offers shares over SMB (Windows, Linux, macOS) or NFS (Linux, Premium only). Mount them as a drive, or cache them on-premises with Azure File Sync.

steps.label: Tiers
steps.title: Choose a tier and a size
body: Standard shares offer transaction optimized, hot and cool tiers. Premium shares run on SSDs in a FileStorage account. A quota caps the share's size.

callout.text: SMB uses TCP port 445, which many home internet providers block.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Containers and shares
body: Blobs for URLs; shares for drives.
recap: Anonymous needs the account setting AND the container level
Standard tiers: transaction optimized, hot, cool; Premium on SSD

handsOn.title: Create a private container and a file share
handsOn.cost: Cents. A few small files in a Standard LRS account cost almost nothing; delete the account at the end.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A storage account in rg-az104-lab: Standard performance, LRS redundancy, default settings. Name it st<yourinitials><number> (lowercase letters and numbers only, globally unique).

steps.do: Open the storage account > Containers > + Container. Name: site, anonymous access level: Private. Create.
steps.see: The site container with access level Private.

steps.do: Upload a small image to site. Open it and copy its URL into a private browser window.
steps.see: An error: the resource is not found or not public.
Blob and Container are greyed out, because the account does not allow anonymous access.

steps.do: Open the account > File shares > + File share. Name: team-drive. Keep the default tier and create.
Open team-drive > Browse > + Add directory: reports. Upload a file into reports.
steps.see: The folder and file in the share.

steps.do: Open team-drive > Edit quota (or Properties) and read the quota setting.
steps.see: The maximum size of the share.

check: The container is private; the share has a folder and a file.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
